title: Red alert for 11 Andhra districts: Schools shut, over 50 trains cancelled as Cyclone Arnab nears landfall - The Times of India

full_text:
VISAKHAPATNAM: As severe Cyclone Arnab is expected to make landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, on Wednesday, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115–125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph, the Andhra Pradesh government has stepped up precautionary measures.
Educational institutions in coastal districts have been closed, sea fishing operations prohibited and rescue teams kept on standby at various locations to ensure zero loss of life and minimal damage to infrastructure.
The rainfall activity with strong gales began in parts of Kakinada, Konaseema, Anakapalle, Visakhapatnam, and a few other districts on Tuesday morning. The locals in Vizag city the sea conditions turned rough on Tuesday morning.
The rainfall activity may intensify from Tuesday afternoon.
The very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” over Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved nearly westwards with a speed of 22 kmph during past six hours, and lay centered 260 km southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 300 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 380 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha), 390 km east of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 460 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh) and 980 km west-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands).
It is very likely to move west-northwestwards till Tuesday (Oct 27) evening. Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Wednesday October (28) afternoon. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on October 27 and 28.
The IMD has issued rainfall warnings of varying severity for coastal Andhra Pradesh and adjoining areas, with the highest level of alert covering several districts on Tuesday and Wednesday.
For Tuesday, a red warning for extremely heavy rainfall has been issued for Anakapalle, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari and Eluru districts, as well as Yanam.
An orange warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall is in force for Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Visakhapatnam, NTR, Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts. A yellow warning for heavy rainfall has been issued for Palnadu, Prakasam and Nellore districts.
For Wednesday, red warnings have been issued for Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalle, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Krishna and Guntur districts.
Orange warnings cover Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram and Bapatla districts, as well as Yanam, while yellow warnings have been issued for Palnadu, Prakasam and Nellore districts.
In view of the imminent cyclone Arnab and in the interest of passenger safety, south coastal railway cancelled more than 50 trains running between Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Kakinada, and few other destinations on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Passengers have been advised to check train-wise cancellation details, confirm their journey dates and verify train status before heading to stations.
The weather conditions associated with cyclone Arnab may impact flights to and from Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada.
However, as of now there are no cancellation of flights from ASR international airport, Bhogapuram and all operations are normal on Tuesday.

title: Cyclone Arnab begins battering coastal Andhra; red alert for five districts - The New Indian Express

full_text:
VISAKHAPATNAM: Rainfall and gusty winds began affecting parts of north coastal Andhra Pradesh early on Tuesday as very severe cyclonic storm Arnab continued moving towards the coast over the west-central Bay of Bengal. The system is expected to intensify through the day, with heavy rainfall forecast in the north coastal districts.
Strong winds and rain began affecting coastal districts, including Srikakulam, Palasa, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam, early on Tuesday. Rainfall also started picking up in the Kakinada-Pithapuram belt.
In its bulletin issued at 2.30 am on Tuesday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said Arnab had moved west-northwestwards at 25 kmph during the preceding six hours.
The storm was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal, around 300 km southeast of Visakhapatnam and 360 km east-southeast of Kakinada.
The IMD has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in Eluru, East Godavari, West Godavari, Konaseema and Kakinada districts. An orange alert has been issued for heavy to very heavy rainfall in Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Bapatla, Guntur, Krishna and NTR districts. Palnadu, Prakasam and Nellore districts are under a yellow alert for moderate to heavy rainfall.
Arnab is likely to continue moving west-northwestwards until Tuesday evening before turning northwestwards. The system is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, by Wednesday forenoon as a very severe cyclonic storm. It is likely to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, with gusts reaching 140 kmph.
Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) managing director Prakhar Jain said the authority was facilitating a faster response to cyclone-related issues through its 'Mana Mitra' WhatsApp service. People can report problems and seek assistance through the number 9552300009.
The authority urged residents in vulnerable areas to follow official advisories and exercise caution as the system approaches the coast.

title: West Bengal Issues Weather Alerts for Heavy Rainfall from Oct 28-30 as Cyclone Arnab Approaches - The CSR Journal

full_text:
West Bengal is set to experience heavy rainfall as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued alerts for several districts from October 28 to 30. The alerts are in response to the impending impact of Cyclone Arnab, which is expected to make landfall near Andhra Pradesh on October 28. The cyclone is projected to bring extremely heavy rainfall to various regions, including West Bengal.
A yellow alert has been declared for several districts in West Bengal on October 28. Areas such as Purulia, Bankura, Jhargram, Purba Medinipur, South 24 Parganas, Birbhum, Paschim Bardhaman, Hooghly, and Nadia are included in this alert. On October 29, the IMD has extended the yellow alert to all districts across the state, indicating widespread rainfall. By October 30, the alert will shift to parts of North Bengal, affecting districts like Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Jalpaiguri, Purba Bardhaman, Nadia, Cooch Behar, Malda, Uttar Dinajpur, and Birbhum.
Impact on Odisha and Other States
The landfall of Cyclone Arnab is expected to cause severe weather conditions in Odisha, particularly in its southern regions. On October 28, an orange alert has been issued for districts including Malkangiri, Koraput, Gajapati, and Ganjam, while a yellow alert is in place for Nabaranhapur, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Khordha, Nayagarh, Puri, Mayurbhanj, Kendujhar, and Cuttack, among others.
On October 29, a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall has been issued for Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Gajapati, and Ganjam. An orange alert will apply to Nabaranhapur, Kalahandi, Nuapara, Balangir, Kandhamal, Khordha, Nayagarh, and Puri, while other areas will remain under a yellow alert. By October 30, the intensity of rainfall is expected to decrease, with only Sundargarh remaining on orange alert.
Manorama Mohanty, the Director of the Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar, has indicated that isolated extremely heavy rainfall and wind speeds of 50 to 60 kmph, with gusts up to 70 kmph, are anticipated in southern Odisha districts. She noted that the cyclone’s path is likely to bring significant rainfall, particularly in hilly areas, raising concerns about potential landslides.
Forecast for Andhra Pradesh
In Andhra Pradesh, heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is expected in North Andhra and Central Coastal districts on October 27 and 28. Areas such as Kakinada, Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Konaseema, and East Godavari are likely to experience strong winds and heavy rainfall. Officials have indicated that the intensity of rainfall will peak on these dates.
The IMD has provided updates regarding Cyclone Arnab, stating that it has intensified from a deep depression into a cyclonic storm over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. The cyclone is expected to move west-northwestwards and further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by the evening of October 26, and into a very severe cyclonic storm by October 27.
The weather department has predicted that Cyclone Arnab will cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of October 28, 2023. Preparations are underway in various states to mitigate the potential impacts of this weather system.

title: At 125 kmph, Cyclone Arnab to hit Andhra coast on Wednesday; schools shut - Rediff
full_text:
Cyclone Arnab, a deep depression in the Bay of Bengal, is rapidly intensifying into a very severe cyclonic storm, posing a significant threat to the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts.
Key Points
- A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclone Arnab.
- Cyclone Arnab is likely to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm by October 27.
- Maximum sustained wind speeds could reach up to 125 kmph with gusts up to 140 kmph.
- Heavy to very heavy rainfall, with extremely heavy rain at isolated places, is forecast for Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on October 27 and 28, with heavy rainfall also likely on October 29.
The eastern coastal states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh closed schools, prohibited sea fishing and kept rescue teams on standby, stepping up precautionary measures ahead of severe Cyclone Arnab's expected landfall on Wednesday to ensure "zero loss of life and minimal damage to infrastructure".
The India meteorological department (IMD) said the deep depression over east-central and southeast Bay of Bengal has moved westward and has intensified into cyclonic storm 'Arnab'.
Cyclone Arnab Intensification
It is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm, with maximum sustained winds of 115-125 kmph gusting up to 140 kmph by the forenoon of October 28, it said.
In the national capital, the National Crisis Management Committee reviewed cyclone preparedness, with cabinet secretary T V Somanathan saying that besides Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Puducherry, the MHA and the IMD should alert eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, since high rainfall was also expected there.
Somanathan asked agencies to ensure zero loss of life and minimal damage to property and infrastructure and directed them that, in the event of any damage, essential services be restored at the earliest.
NDRF Deploys Teams
The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) informed the meeting that they have deployed teams, with additional teams on standby.
"Rescue and relief teams of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Indian Coast Guard, along with their ships and aircraft, have been kept ready. Indian Coast Guard has so far shepherded multiple ships/boats to jetties/shore, and the remaining ships have been alerted to return to the coast," a government statement said.
While the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have ordered the closure of all schools till Tuesday, the Odisha government shuttered schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres in six southern Odisha districts of Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput and Nabarangpur on October 28 and 29.
In view of inclement weather conditions, the state prohibited fishing activities in the sea, stopped entry of tourists in the hills, waterfalls and dams in the six districts and started moving people from vulnerable areas to safety.
Odisha CM Deputes 8 Ministers
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi deputed eight ministers at separate places to monitor pre-cyclone activities.
He said that though the severe cyclonic storm is likely to make landfall between Andhra Pradesh and Yanam in Puducherry, Odisha would be heavily impacted, witnessing very heavy rainfall and winds gusting up to 80 kmph.
Rescue teams, comprising personnel of the NDRF, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), the Fire and Emergency Services and the police, have been pre-positioned at vulnerable areas.
"People living in thatched houses and low-lying areas are being shifted to shelters. Pregnant women are being taken to health centres in advance. Special arrangements are also in place for senior citizens, children, and persons with disabilities," Odisha's disaster management minister Suresh Pujari said.
Andhra Releases Rs 27 cr for Relief Ops
He said all cyclone centres, along with some temporary ones, have been readied. The state government has cancelled leave of its employees in the identified districts, and control rooms have been opened to coordinate relief and rescue operations.
The agriculture department has advised farmers to harvest and safely store crops that are 80-85 percent mature. Dedicated agricultural helpline numbers have been opened for assistance, the minister added.
The Andhra Pradesh government released Rs 27 crore to 20 districts for relief operations. Rs 2 crore each have been released to Bapatla, Krishna, Konaseema, East and West Godavari, Kakinada and Anakapalli districts for relief and response measures, a release from Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority said.
Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed cyclone preparedness with officials and instructed them to alert people according to the likely impact of the weather system and take all necessary steps to minimise damage.
He directed them to analyse information from previous cyclones and issue timely warnings to farmers and the public to help them take necessary precautions.
Beaches, Coastal Roads Closed for Public Safety
Educational institutions in cyclone-affected areas have been declared closed. Beaches have been closed to the public, while movement on coastal roads is scheduled to be suspended from Tuesday afternoon to ensure public safety.
Officials informed the chief minister that arrangements were underway to shift 4,711 identified pregnant women from vulnerable areas to primary health centres, community health centres and hospitals, while all fishermen who had ventured into the sea had returned safely.
As many as 15 NDRF teams have been stationed across Kakinada, Nadipudi in Amalapuram, Konaseema, Rajahmundry in East Godavari, Eluru, Narsapuram in West Godavari, Machilipatnam in Krishna district and Nakkapalli in Anakapalli district.
Of these teams, two have been deployed at Yanam while three each are stationed at the NDRF Battalion Headquarters in Krishna district and the Regional Response Centre in Visakhapatnam.
Officials estimate that Tandava, Raiwada, Yeleru, Tammileru, Yerrakalava and Tadipudi reservoirs could reach their full storage capacities following the rainfall predicted to be caused by the cyclone.
Naidu instructed officials to ensure adequate stocks of essential commodities at ration shops and restore electricity supply immediately wherever disruptions occurred.
Heavy Rain Likely in Bengal From Oct 28 to 30
The cyclone is likely to bring heavy rain in several districts of West Bengal from October 28 to 30, the IMD predicted and advised fishermen not to venture into the sea along and off the West Bengal coast from Monday, as squally winds will prevail over the region.
It also warned of possible landslides in the sub-Himalayan district of Darjeeling in the wake of the cyclone. The sub-Himalayan districts of Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Alipurduar and Jalpaiguri could receive heavy rain on October 29 and October 30.
